Mecka AI is building the data infrastructure layer for robotics and embodied AI.

We work closely with frontier robotics teams to bridge real-world data, simulation, learning-based systems, and deployed hardware.
The Role
We are hiring a Software Developer to build — end to end — the internal products and tooling that turn Mecka’s ego-data pipeline into fast, reliable, at-spec dataset deliveries to frontier AI labs. This is a 0→1 role: you’ll take a rough delivery problem, design the interface and the system behind it, ship a first version fast, and iterate with the people using it.
You’ll own whole surfaces rather than a single layer — the review and QA UIs our labeling and delivery teams live in, the dashboards sales uses to track a delivery, the export and validation logic underneath, and the data plumbing that ties it together. Front-end one week, data pipeline the next, a scrappy internal tool the week after.
You’ll work hand-in-hand with the Delivery Operations team — including our Robotic Data & Deliveries TPM — turning recurring delivery pain into products people actually want to use. When a workflow is slow, manual, or fragile, you’re the one who builds the thing that fixes it.
Ideal background: full-stack or product engineering with a track record of building tools and products 0→1. Comfort with data and large-dataset systems is a strong plus, but breadth, product sense, and speed matter more than depth in any one stack.
What you will be doing:
Internal Products & Delivery Tooling
Design and build the internal products our teams use every day — dataset review and QA interfaces, delivery-tracking dashboards, data viewers, and the workflows that string them together — owning both the UI and the logic behind it.
Turn one-off scripts and manual steps into real tools with a usable interface, so delivery, sales, labeling, and QA move faster without engineering babysitting.
0→1 Product Building
Take fuzzy problems from a conversation to a shipped v1 quickly, then iterate with real users — internal teams today, and the experience AI-lab customers touch when they receive a delivery.
Make pragmatic build-vs-buy and scope calls; ship the 80% that unblocks people now and harden it as it proves out.
Data & Platform Plumbing
Build the pipelines and APIs that package, validate, index, and serve ego datasets — the systems that make petabyte-scale video and sensor data usable for delivery, labeling, QA, and model training.
Keep the tools you ship reliable and honest about data quality, so problems get caught before a dataset reaches a customer.
Who You Are
3+ years building software as a full-stack or product engineer (or equivalent impact) — you’re comfortable owning a feature from UI to data.
Fluent in a modern front-end stack (e.g., TypeScript/React) and at least one backend language (e.g., Python, Node, Go).
A demonstrated 0→1 builder — you’ve taken tools or products from nothing to in-use, and you thrive in ambiguity without a detailed spec.
Strong product sense and a bias to ship: you scope ruthlessly, get a v1 in front of users, and iterate.
Comfortable working directly with data — querying databases (e.g., SQL, MongoDB) and reshaping or validating datasets.
Even better if you have:
You’ve been an early or founding engineer, built internal tools teams loved, or shipped side projects end to end.
You have real UX/design instincts — your tools are fast, clear, and pleasant to use, not just functional.
You think in terms of the user, clean interfaces, and shipping — and you write maintainable code with strong ownership.
Exposure to video/media or large-dataset systems (ingestion, storage, metadata/search, ETL) is a plus, not a requirement.
Why This Role
Own real surface area from day one — build the products that power petabyte-scale robotics datasets and the deliveries frontier AI labs depend on.
Maximum breadth: front-end, back-end, data, and product, on problems that are still greenfield.
High ownership and direct impact across delivery, operations, sales, and research — paired tightly with the TPM who owns the delivery programs you build for.

description_preview:
Please note that this position is based on our campus in Madison, WI, and requires relocation to the area. We recruit nationally and provide financial relocation assistance.
Code that saves lives.
As a software developer at Epic, you’ll write software that impacts the lives of 325 million patients around the world. Working in your own office, surrounded by thousands of high-caliber developers, you’ll use modern development methodologies and employ user-centered design, analytics, and machine learning tools to drive innovation in healthcare. Using leading-edge technologies and languages like JS, TS, and C#, you’ll invent better ways to reduce medical errors, streamline record sharing between hospitals, and provide the quality of care a patient deserves. Learn more about our team at https://careers.epic.com/jobs/softwaredevelopment/.
Write software for the most innovative health systems on the planet.
The top-ranked health systems in U.S. News and World Report are Epic customers. Our community includes major systems like the Mayo Clinic, Johns Hopkins, Cleveland Clinic, and Kaiser Permanente, as well as leading academic medical centers at the University of Wisconsin, University of Michigan, University of California, University of Texas, The Ohio State University, and many more.
Live affordably in a city known for its rising tech talent.
Epic is located just outside Madison, Wisconsin, the second fastest growing market for tech talent in the United States and home to the state capital and the University of Wisconsin. Madison, a city surrounded by water, has received accolades for being the greenest city in America (NerdWallet), the best city for renters (SmartAsset), the fittest city in America (Fitbit), and the third best metro in the US for young professionals (Forbes Advisor).
More than just important work
.
Our uniquely themed campus was designed to heighten your ability to get stuff done in your office, a conference room, or by the fireplace in a comfy chair. All meals are restaurant-quality but cost only a few dollars, and they’re prepared by a team comprised of kitchen talent from restaurants around the country. And, after five years here, you’ll earn a four-week sabbatical anywhere in the world. Staff have kayaked in Patagonia, attended a Beyoncé concert in Ireland, built a library in Tanzania, and run a marathon in Antarctica.
We offer comprehensive benefits to keep you healthy and happy as you grow in your life and career, and your merit-based compensation will reflect the impact your work has on the company and our customers. You'll also be eligible for annual raises and bonuses, as well as stock grants, which give you an even greater stake in the success of Epic and our customers. Healthcare is global, and building the best ideas from around the world into Epic software is a point of pride. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we know that inclusive teams design software that supports the delivery of quality care for all patients, so diversity, equity, and inclusion are written into our principles. Please see our full non-discrimination statement at https://careers.epic.com/EEO.
Relocation to the Madison, WI area (Reimbursed)
BS/BA or greater in Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field
A history of academic excellence or professional success
Eligible to work in the United States without visa sponsorship (persons with appropriate qualifications and eligible for TN status under NAFTA may apply)
COVID-19 vaccination

reason: Stack +17; Title fit +12; Entry +15; Exp fit +10; US +10
description_preview:
Join our growing team and discover why Summit Utilities, Inc. continues to earn national and regional recognition as an employer of choice. Our recognitions include Best Places to Work in Maine (2019–2025); Best Places to Work in Arkansas (2020, 2023, 2025); Best Places to Work in Oklahoma (2022–2025); Best Places to Work in Missouri (2023 and 2026); Best Places to Work in Colorado (2025); Forbes America’s Best Small Employers (2023); and, most recently, Proud and Purposeful Employer (2026).
Summit is a growing natural gas utility providing safe, reliable, and clean burning natural gas service to homes and businesses in Arkansas, Colorado, Maine, Missouri, Oklahoma, and Texas. Being part of the Summit team means embracing excellence and innovation, committing to safety each and every day, and doing all that we can to serve each other, our customers, and the communities where we live. We aim to bring warmth and energy to everything we do.
We have an exciting opportunity for a a Data Engineer I (SGL17). This hybrid role can be based in one of our offices in Fort Smith, Fayetteville, or Little Rock, Arkansas.
POSITION SUMMARY
Summit Utilities is seeking a
Data Engineer I
to support the development, maintenance, and enhancement of enterprise data pipelines and integration solutions. This entry-level engineering role is ideal for professionals with foundational experience in data systems and a strong interest in growing their expertise within a collaborative, enterprise-scale environment. The Data Engineer I works closely with senior engineers, analysts, and database administrators to implement and support reliable data solutions across platforms. Ideal candidates have 1–3 years of experience with ETL development, SQL scripting, and modern data integration practices, along with a demonstrated sense of ownership, curiosity, and attention to detail when working with complex data environments.
PRIMARY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Build and maintain scalable, reliable data pipelines and integration workflows using modern orchestration tools, low-code platforms, and custom scripting across on-prem and cloud systems.
Ingest, transform, and stage structured and semi-structured data into enterprise data repositories, including writing, troubleshooting, and optimizing SQL queries, views, and stored procedures.
Support data quality and reliability by implementing validation checks, alerts, logging, and monitoring, and by partnering with Data Analysts and SAP Analysts to validate datasets and confirm accurate delivery.
Document data sources, pipeline logic, and transformations in shared repositories, and manage code through team-based source control and code review practices.
Participate in standups, sprint planning, and on-call rotations, responding to data support tickets and identifying opportunities to improve processes and adopt new technologies.
EDUCATION AND WORK EXPERIENCE
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field preferred; equivalent combination of education and relevant experience will be considered.
1–3 years of experience in data engineering, ETL development, or data integration roles
Experience building or maintaining data pipelines using orchestration tools and/or custom scripting.
Practical experience with relational databases, including writing and tuning SQL, plus exposure to cloud-based data environments and collaborative source control.
KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES
Working knowledge of modern data orchestration and workflow automation tools, including building pipelines with both low-code platforms and custom code
Solid understanding of relational databases with the ability to write and debug T-SQL or PL/SQL; exposure to cloud data engineering concepts preferred.
Understanding of data integration concepts, including file transfers (FTP/SFTP), API-based ingestion, data staging, source control, and deployment automation
Strong problem-solving and analytical skills with attention to data accuracy and reliability, and the ability to document processes, logic flows, and system configurations clearly.
Effective verbal and written communication with analysts, engineers, and stakeholders; self-motivated, team-oriented, and aligned with PEAKS values and organizational goals.
The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this classification. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and/or skills required of all personnel so classified.
Summit offers competitive pay and medical/dental/vision and other benefits that provide flexibility, choice, and support to our employees when they need it most. We understand that home and family are essential pieces of your life, and our benefits are designed to support you both at work and at home.
Summit Utilities, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability or veteran status.

description_preview:
Join our growing team and discover why Summit Utilities, Inc. continues to earn national and regional recognition as an employer of choice. Our recognitions include Best Places to Work in Maine (2019–2025); Best Places to Work in Arkansas (2020, 2023, 2025); Best Places to Work in Oklahoma (2022–2025); Best Places to Work in Missouri (2023 and 2026); Best Places to Work in Colorado (2025); Forbes America’s Best Small Employers (2023); and, most recently, Proud and Purposeful Employer (2026).
Summit is a growing natural gas utility providing safe, reliable, and clean burning natural gas service to homes and businesses in Arkansas, Colorado, Maine, Missouri, Oklahoma, and Texas. Being part of the Summit team means embracing excellence and innovation, committing to safety each and every day, and doing all that we can to serve each other, our customers, and the communities where we live. We aim to bring warmth and energy to everything we do.
We have an exciting opportunity for a a Data Engineer I (SGL17). This hybrid role can be based in one of our offices in Fort Smith, Fayetteville, or Little Rock, Arkansas.
POSITION SUMMARY
Summit Utilities is seeking a
Data Engineer I
to support the development, maintenance, and enhancement of enterprise data pipelines and integration solutions. This entry-level engineering role is ideal for professionals with foundational experience in data systems and a strong interest in growing their expertise within a collaborative, enterprise-scale environment. The Data Engineer I works closely with senior engineers, analysts, and database administrators to implement and support reliable data solutions across platforms. Ideal candidates have 1–3 years of experience with ETL development, SQL scripting, and modern data integration practices, along with a demonstrated sense of ownership, curiosity, and attention to detail when working with complex data environments.
PRIMARY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Build and maintain scalable, reliable data pipelines and integration workflows using modern orchestration tools, low-code platforms, and custom scripting across on-prem and cloud systems.
Ingest, transform, and stage structured and semi-structured data into enterprise data repositories, including writing, troubleshooting, and optimizing SQL queries, views, and stored procedures.
Support data quality and reliability by implementing validation checks, alerts, logging, and monitoring, and by partnering with Data Analysts and SAP Analysts to validate datasets and confirm accurate delivery.
Document data sources, pipeline logic, and transformations in shared repositories, and manage code through team-based source control and code review practices.
Participate in standups, sprint planning, and on-call rotations, responding to data support tickets and identifying opportunities to improve processes and adopt new technologies.
EDUCATION AND WORK EXPERIENCE
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field preferred; equivalent combination of education and relevant experience will be considered.
1–3 years of experience in data engineering, ETL development, or data integration roles
Experience building or maintaining data pipelines using orchestration tools and/or custom scripting.
Practical experience with relational databases, including writing and tuning SQL, plus exposure to cloud-based data environments and collaborative source control.
KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES
Working knowledge of modern data orchestration and workflow automation tools, including building pipelines with both low-code platforms and custom code
Solid understanding of relational databases with the ability to write and debug T-SQL or PL/SQL; exposure to cloud data engineering concepts preferred.
Understanding of data integration concepts, including file transfers (FTP/SFTP), API-based ingestion, data staging, source control, and deployment automation
Strong problem-solving and analytical skills with attention to data accuracy and reliability, and the ability to document processes, logic flows, and system configurations clearly.
Effective verbal and written communication with analysts, engineers, and stakeholders; self-motivated, team-oriented, and aligned with PEAKS values and organizational goals.
The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this classification. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and/or skills required of all personnel so classified.
Summit offers competitive pay and medical/dental/vision and other benefits that provide flexibility, choice, and support to our employees when they need it most. We understand that home and family are essential pieces of your life, and our benefits are designed to support you both at work and at home.
Summit Utilities, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability or veteran status.

description_preview:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
About The Team
At Anduril, our Battlespace Awareness Command and Control Software team specializes in solving complex, real-world problems through cutting-edge algorithms and intelligent software integrations. Operating in small, innovative teams, we push the boundaries of what's possible to deliver advanced technologies with mission-critical applications. Our commitment doesn't end with academic research or proof-of-concept experiments; we measure our success by the real-world impact of our deployed solutions. Inspired by Arthur C. Clarke's vision — “Any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic” — we aim to achieve groundbreaking results in path planning, route optimization, and autonomous mission execution at the command and control layer. We are currently seeking highly talented technologists to join our mission and redefine the future of defense technology.
What You Will Do
Contribute hands-on to a small, collaborative team within the Command and Control Software organization, applying your growing expertise in path planning and route optimization.
Prototype and help deploy state-of-the-art algorithms for global and local path planning, trajectory optimization, and multi-agent coordination within command and control systems.
Help develop online (real-time) path planning capabilities that replan safely and efficiently as mission conditions, threats, and vehicle states change.
Design and develop high-performance software for real-time C2 systems deployed on operational platforms in the field — from operator-facing mission planning tools to autonomous tasking and routing services that orchestrate fleets of unmanned systems — with a strong emphasis on asynchronous programming, concurrency, and reliable execution in resource-constrained environments.
Implement robust planners, search algorithms, and decision-making systems that generate safe, feasible, and optimal routes in dynamic, uncertain, and contested environments.
Analyze system performance using high-fidelity simulations, modeling tools, and statistical techniques to validate planner behavior across diverse mission scenarios.
Support customer success by developing and implementing algorithms and software for mission-critical use cases, including collaborative autonomy, asset routing, and obstacle and threat avoidance.
Integrate path planning technologies into the broader command and control software stack and development lifecycle, from requirements definition through testing and optimization.
Translate technical progress into clear, actionable insights for diverse stakeholders, including colleagues, operators, and end-users.
Required Qualifications
3+ years of experience in algorithm design, software development, and mathematical modeling with programming expertise in C/C++ and/or Rust.
Strong knowledge of path planning techniques, such as graph-based search (A*, D* Lite), sampling-based planners (RRT, RRT*, PRM), and online/real-time replanning approaches.
Demonstrated experience in guidance, navigation, and control (GNC); trajectory optimization and trajectory prediction; and/or the development of predictive models for vehicle dynamics and weapon system effectiveness (e.g., 6-DoF simulation, intercept analysis).
Solid understanding of applied mathematics, including linear algebra, optimization, computational geometry, and graph theory.
Knowledge of vehicle dynamics, kinematic constraints, and control theory as applied to autonomous ground, air, or maritime platforms tasked through C2 systems, including high-speed aerial vehicles.
Familiarity with map representations, terrain reasoning, state estimation, and the efficient handling of large-scale geospatial and environmental data within distributed C2 architectures.
Exposure to machine learning as applied to planning and decision-making, including reinforcement learning, learned heuristics, and behavior prediction.
Ability to write robust, concurrent code for planning under uncertainty and operation in complex, dynamic, contested environments.
Demonstrated ability to work across development lifecycles, from prototyping to optimizing production systems.
Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.
NICE TO HAVE
Experience with Rust for high-performance, safety-critical software.
Exposure to mixed greenfield/brownfield codebases, including extending an existing planning/routing stack in production.

Transcripts help us assess your technical and analytical abilities, complementing our interview process in which we also evaluate practical experience and cultural fit. If you're energized by velocity, obsessed with raising the bar, and want to build alongside people who care deeply about each other and our customers, we'd love to meet you.
About The Role
We're looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer to own solution design and implementation for our Identity Resolution (IDR) product. This role is a blend of data analytics and data engineering, and is an opportunity to work directly with data, marketing, and executive teams at household-name companies. You'll spend time working with the customer to learn about their data architecture, reason about how Hightouch can accomplish their goals, set up deployments, and debug issues.
This role is hands on and technical. You’ll become intimately familiar with our customers’ data and business goals. This expertise frequently leads to us advising executives at Fortune 500 companies on their long term data strategy. You'll spend time helping customers decide how their global identity spines should be configured, you'll set up implementations for them, and you'll debug inevitable issues with real data. You'll work closely with Sales Engineering on pre-sales deals and with Customer Support Engineering and Technical Account Management on post-sales implementations—serving as the subject matter expert for data engineering and analytics across the customer lifecycle.
You'll work with coding agents as a default: the SQL, schema spelunking, and internal tooling in this role gets built with agents - and you’ll help grow our repository of skills and best practices so we all get faster.
About Hightouch Identity Resolution (IDR)
Imagine you're a sprawling enterprise business with 20+ brands. Each brand collects different data elements from each of their customers and joins using different identifiers. Hightouch IDR can look across the customer data stored in each brand and provide a golden source of truth using all the available data, while obeying any regulatory restrictions that prevent data sharing. The product is highly configurable, and so no two customer data architectures are the same.
What You'll Do
Solution Architecture & Implementation Consulting
Work backwards from end goals: Customers ultimately don't care about IDR itself, but about the use cases that a good identity spine powers. You’ll pair with an architect to work backwards from the customer’s use cases to a set of IDR rules and a data model that enables those use cases
Assess fit and feasibility: During pre-sales, understand the customer’s data landscape and maturity, assessing how much work will be needed to get their data ready for IDR. Understand the rules of any current solutions (e.g., Reltio, Amperity, Segment, MDM tools) and identify, flag, and create workarounds for any gaps.
Technical Support & Debugging
Debug customer issues end-to-end: Investigate perceived issues and discrepancies in identity such as missing datapoints and over-merging scenarios. Most debugging involves writing SQL against customer warehouses and reading server logs.
Explain IDR behavior to customers: Help customers understand how warehouse-native identity resolution works and detailed nuances of how it processes data incrementally or how to utilize its outcome tables.
Surface product gaps: When you see the same issue repeatedly (e.g., no retroactive data removal, insufficient observability into profile changes, inability to reset incremental processing watermarks), flag and advocate for fixes.
What We're Looking For
You direct agents, you don't just prompt them. You'll point them at warehouses with undocumented tables and no reliable dictionary, and you'll be the last judgment before what they build ships to millions of people. You reach for an agent before a blank editor, but you scrutinize every line before it goes out.
SQL Fluency: Anyone can generate a thousand lines of SQL now. You're hired because you can read them and find the join that's wrong. Fluent in Snowflake, Databricks or BigQuery, with query performance and warehouse cost as things you think about unprompted.
Systems thinking: You can reason about how identity graphs behave at scale, understand trade-offs between different architecture choices, and anticipate downstream consequences of design decisions.
Consultative communication: You can run a discovery call, ask the right questions to understand requirements, and explain technical trade-offs to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Systematic debugging mindset: You naturally form hypotheses, test them, and document findings. When you see "missing data," you think through timestamps, model definitions, and PK validity before jumping to conclusions.
2-4 years in an analytics engineering, solutions engineering, forward-deployed engineering, or implementation role—ideally at a data infrastructure, CDP, or B2B SaaS company.
Nice to Have
Experience with identity resolution, MDM, or CDP products (Segment, Amperity, Reltio, LiveRamp)
Familiarity with graph data structures and entity resolution algorithms

Astrocade is an AI technology company building super-intelligence for the interactive world, delivered through a breakout consumer platform.
Today's frontier models can write, reason, and generate video. None can build a world you can step into and act on. Interactive world models are one of the defining problems on the path to ASI, and the foundation of the next great consumer platform. Interactivity is the holy grail of content: not something you watch, but something that responds to you. We're further ahead than anyone: the only team building the intelligence and the platform together, and both are already live.
Our social UGC platform lets anyone create and play interactive experiences through natural language. And it's one of the fastest-growing consumer products in the world, with over 30 million users in just months since launch. Creators bring to life games, companions that remember and grow with them, learning experiences that adapt like a great tutor, and social worlds built with friends. The platform also powers our research with data no video dataset contains: millions of creators prompting and refining gives us paired data of human intent and the worlds that fulfill it, and every play session produces ground-truth, action-labeled interaction data at scale. All of it flows back into our models, and research ships to real players in days, spinning a flywheel no one else can build.
We are a small team from Google Research, Meta, FAIR, Character.ai, and Stanford, led alongside Fei-Fei Li, with frontier-scale compute and direct ownership of core model problems. We are backed by Sequoia Capital, Google, NVIDIA, and luminaries including Eric Schmidt and Jerry Yang.

About The Role
Every experience on Astrocade starts as an idea from a creator. An agentic AI system turns that idea into something playable. How good that experience turns out to be is our north-star metric. Your job is to move that metric.
As an ML Engineer on our AI team, you'll own how our creation system behaves, where it fails, and how it gets better. You'll dig into real creator sessions to find where generation breaks down, build the evals that tell us whether a change actually helped, and design the agentic systems behind the next version of creation on the platform. This is applied ML with a direct line to product. What you ship shows up in the games millions of players see.
We're a small team of about 20 engineers, and nobody here stays in a lane. You'll work across models, agents, data pipelines, and infrastructure as the problem requires, and you'll collaborate directly with our CTO and co-founders.

Have 3–7+ years of experience in ML engineering or applied ML, with a track record of shipping models or AI systems to real users

description_preview:
About The Team
We build the cloud-native software that thousands of rental businesses around the world run on every day — the rental management platform and the e-commerce suite that sits on top of it.
This role is how we bring new engineers into that work. You'll start where the whole system is visible: verifying, breaking, and instrumenting the product before a customer ever sees it. That vantage point is one of the fastest ways there is to learn a large codebase and a complicated domain at the same time. And you'll be writing code from your first sprint — reading it, fixing it, shipping it alongside the developers, not filing tickets over a wall at them.
We built this role deliberately as an entry point for people early in their engineering careers.
What you'll do
Write code from your first sprint
Write and maintain automated tests in the same repositories and the same languages as the product — JavaScript and TypeScript against our Angular front ends and Node/NestJS services, PHP where our longer-standing surfaces live
Read the codebase to work out why something broke, not just that it broke
Fix low-risk defects yourself and take them through code review like any other engineer
Build the small internal tools and scripts that make the team's testing and release process faster
Take on scoped product work under a mentor's review as you ramp
Do the quality work that teaches you the system
Verify new features and fixes across our web and desktop products, and write bug reports a developer can act on immediately
Build and maintain test plans for new features alongside senior engineers
Run regression passes so a new release doesn't break what already worked
Partner with developers and product managers to understand requirements and flag gaps early
Take part in release readiness reviews
What you bring
You can write and read code in at least one language. We care that you can build something and explain the choices you made — not which stack you learned on.
Something we can look at: a capstone, a bootcamp project, a personal project, a GitHub profile, or work from a previous role
A foundation in software development or testing, through a degree, a coding bootcamp, a self-taught path, an internship, or early professional experience
Strong written communication — your bug reports and your commit messages both tell the whole story
Curiosity about how systems break, and the patience to chase an edge case down to its root cause
A working understanding of the software development lifecycle and where quality sits in it
Preferred, not required: exposure to Playwright, Selenium, Cypress or similar; SQL; REST APIs; Azure DevOps or Jira; SaaS products
Who this role is for. You might be arriving from a CS degree, a coding bootcamp, a self-taught path, the military, or a completely different career. You might already work at Point of Rental in support, implementation, or professional services and want to move into engineering — if you know the rental business cold, you already have the half of this job that takes longest to teach. All of those are the point of this role.
How you'll grow
The path from this role is to Full Stack Engineer. That's the destination, and the role is built to get you there.
Start here. Learn the product and the domain. Own exploratory and release testing. Get fluent in our codebase, our tooling, and how we ship.
Then. Write automated tests in the product repositories. Fix defects and take your code through review. Build the internal tooling your team runs on.
Then. Take scoped feature work under mentorship — front end, services, and data — until you're carrying it on your own.
You'll have a named mentor, regular one-on-ones, code review used as a teaching tool, and dedicated learning time every week. We promote on demonstrated ability rather than on a calendar, but the destination is written down and your manager's job is to get you to it.
Why Point of Rental
Point of Rental is the global leader in rental software. The code you write here shows up in equipment yards, event companies, and job sites on six continents, in the hands of people who notice immediately when something is wrong.
You'll be an engineer from day one — in the repositories, in code review, in the room with the developers and product managers shipping the product. We opened this role because we would rather build engineers than only buy them.
